 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 04.02.2022 passed by IV Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Member MACT No.XV, Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.823/2019, this appeal is filed.

sentences.text: 2. Sri Koujalagi Chandrakanth Laxman, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimants, seeking for enhancement of compensation on limited ground insofar as award under coventional heads.
It was submitted NC: 2023:KHC-K:6390 that at time of accident, Basavaraj was aged 63 years, working as agriculturist and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.

Tribunal by considering his monthly income notionally at Rs.13,250/-, deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and applying multiplier of 7, awarded compensation of Rs.7,42,056/- towards loss of dependency.
However, it awarded inadequate compensation towards loss of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate, which called for enhancement.

sentences.text: 3. On other hand, Sri Sudarshan M., learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer sought to justify award.

4. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
5.

From above submission, since insurer has not preferred appeal, finding of Tribunal regarding occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to rash and negligent driving thereof by its driver leading to death of Basavaraj, issuance of insurance policy and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.

Since claimants are in appeal for enhancement of compensation,
point that arises for consideration is:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6390 "Whether appellants/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
6.

In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v.
Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, claimants would be entitled for award of consortium at Rs.40,000/- each i.e., claimant no.1-wife would be entitled for loss of spousal consortium at Rs.40,000/-; claimants no.2 and 3-sons would be entitled for loss of filial consortium at Rs.40,000/- each.

sentences.text: In addition, claimants would be entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Since more than three years have lapsed after rendering of decision in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), they would be entiteld for addition of 10% i.e., Rs.15,000/-.
Thus, in addition to award of Rs.7,42,056/- towards loss of dependency, claimants would be entitled for addition of Rs.1,65,000/- under conventional heads.
Thereby, total compensation would be Rs.9,07,056/-.
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.
 ii.
Appellants/claimants are entitled for total  compensation of Rs.9,07,056/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Respondent no.2-insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. On deposit, entire compensation insofar as conventional heads is ordered to be released in favour of claimants.
